name: clean-code
description: Robert C. Martin's Clean Code as five routing knowledge-base skills, one per language family, that cover any language between them. Each is a chaptered reference — rules, worked examples, a cheatsheet, a glossary and a pattern catalogue — and each description routes to the right sibling, so the model loads the one skill that fits the file it is editing. clean-code-java carries the original book (Java examples, the refactoring case studies, and the 66-item smells-and-heuristics catalogue); clean-code-typescript, clean-code-javascript and clean-code-python carry the community adaptations, each worked in its own idiom — TS types and Failable results, JS closures and promises, Python ABCs, dataclasses and mypy. clean-code-universal is the family's shared core: a language-agnostic distillation cross-checked against all four, built on a three-tier spine that separates rules holding wherever you can name a thing and run a check (Tier 1) from rules binding only where a construct exists — a parameter list, a type system, an exception, a test runner, a thread (Tier 2). It carries the languages the book never covers: Go, Rust, C#, C++, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Scala, and the declarative ones — YAML (Kubernetes, Helm, CI pipelines), Terraform/HCL, SQL, Bash, Dockerfile — with a translation table stating, per rule, what it means where there are no functions, no classes and no unit tests, and which rules genuinely do not apply. Sources and licences differ per skill: see NOTICE.md.
